summary: Banking ledger core and CLI: accounts in integer cents, queued transfers with settlement, daily spend limits, fees, interest and statements, persisted to a text state file.

defects.anchor: (balance_cents as f64 * rate_bp as f64 / 10_000.0) as i64
defects.title: Interest computed in f64 truncates cents
defects.description: accrue_interest converts the cent balance to f64 before multiplying, so large balances lose representable precision and the truncation drops a cent versus exact integer arithmetic.
defects.trigger: interest on an account holding 9388934101589121 cents at 500 bp
defects.observed: credits 469446705079455 cents while exact integer math gives 469446705079456.

defects.title: Daily allowance underflows when spent exceeds limit
defects.description: remaining_daily_allowance subtracts spent from limit with wrapping_sub; once fees push spent_today above the limit the allowance wraps to ~1.8e19 and every later transfer passes the daily-limit check.
defects.trigger: open with limit 500, charge a 600-cent fee, then statement / transfer
defects.observed: statement prints remaining_daily_allowance 18446744073709551516; a 5000-cent transfer is approved (release profile, wraps silently).

defects.title: Transfer accepts negative amounts
defects.description: request_transfer only checks balance >= amount, so a negative amount always passes and at settlement moves money from the destination into the source.
defects.observed: a goes 1000->1500 and b goes 2000->1500 after transferring -500.

defects.title: Split divides by empty recipient list
defects.description: split_payment divides the amount by recipients.len() with no empty check, so an empty recipient list panics on integer division by zero.
defects.observed: process panics with 'attempt to divide by zero', exit 101.

defects.title: Account index used without bounds check
defects.description: account_at indexes self.accounts with a CLI-supplied index and no length check.
defects.observed: index out of bounds panic, exit 101.

defects.title: Rejected transfer resets the daily spend counter
defects.description: The running spend total is reset inside the over-limit rejection branch instead of on a day change, so alternating an accepted and a rejected transfer lets total settled spend exceed the daily limit.
defects.observed: 1200 cents settle against a daily limit of 1000.

defects.title: Closing an account leaves queued transfers that settle into it
defects.description: close_account only flips the closed flag; pending transfers referencing the account stay queued and settle() credits a closed account.
defects.trigger: transfer a b 400; close b; settle

defects.title: Audit log grows without bound
defects.description: record_audit appends to the in-memory audit Vec on every operation and nothing trims it; the history-lines constant is only used to limit statement display.
defects.observed: audit entries=5001 and the state file grows to ~70 KB; entries are never dropped.

defects.title: Amount parsing unwraps user input
defects.description: parse_cents unwraps the CLI parse result, so a non-numeric amount panics instead of producing a usage error.

defects.title: Operator token hardcoded in source
defects.description: The privileged adjust/close commands compare --token against OPERATOR_TOKEN (env override falls back to the compiled-in constant), so anyone who can read the binary/source can run operator commands.
defects.observed: adjust succeeds with the built-in token, balance 100->5100.

defects.title: Statement --out joins user path onto reports dir
defects.description: write_statement joins the --out name onto reports/ without normalising or rejecting '..', so a crafted name writes the statement outside the reports directory.
defects.observed: statement file is written to a directory outside reports/.
